sources: Current Oracle text in current-cycle Scryfall cache
Magic Comprehensive Rules — activated abilities, targets, combat, copying abilities, Aura targeting, MDFCs, overload and landfall (current 2026 rules)

interactions.name: Tetsuo target condition
interactions.finding: Tetsuo may target a creature that is tapped OR a creature that is currently blocking. The target need not satisfy both. When the ability resolves the target must still satisfy at least one of those target restrictions or that instance of the ability will not resolve against it.

interactions.name: Attacking creates tapped targets
interactions.finding: A creature without vigilance normally becomes tapped as it is declared as an attacker. After attackers are declared, Tetsuo may be activated before blockers/combat damage and can target an attacker that is tapped.

interactions.name: Blocking condition
interactions.finding: After blockers are declared, a blocking creature is a legal Tetsuo target even if it is untapped.

interactions.name: Rings plus Illusionist Bracers
interactions.finding: Activating Tetsuo can trigger both Rings of Brighthearth and Illusionist’s Bracers. Bracers copies the nonmana activated ability; Rings may also copy it for {2}. If both copy effects are used, the original plus two copies can resolve with new targets chosen for the copies.

interactions.name: Untap and reactivate
interactions.finding: Untapping Tetsuo after activating does not remove the existing activation from the stack. If UBBR can be paid again, Tetsuo can be activated again after being untapped.

interactions.name: Patriars Seal
interactions.finding: Patriar’s Seal either taps for one mana of any color or can pay {1} and tap to untap target legendary creature you control, including Tetsuo. The same untapped Seal cannot perform both tap-cost abilities at once.

interactions.name: Puppeteer
interactions.finding: Puppeteer may tap an opposing creature to create a Tetsuo target or untap Tetsuo for another activation.

interactions.name: Flood
interactions.finding: Flood pays UU to tap target creature without flying. A creature successfully tapped this way satisfies Tetsuo’s tapped target condition.

interactions.name: Blustersquall overload
interactions.finding: Normal Blustersquall taps one opposing creature. When overloaded for 3U, target is replaced by each, so it does not target and taps each creature the caster does not control, creating multiple potential Tetsuo targets.

interactions.name: Retreat to Coralhelm and fetchlands
interactions.finding: Each land entering under your control triggers Retreat. A fetchland entering can create one trigger and the fetched land entering creates another. Each trigger may tap or untap target creature, allowing target creation or Tetsuo reuse.

interactions.name: Aura restriction
interactions.finding: Tetsuo cannot be the target of Aura spells. Equipment, non-Aura abilities such as Minamo, Puppeteer, Patriar’s Seal and Retreat to Coralhelm, and Tetsuo’s own activation are not prohibited by that text.

interactions.name: Haste equipment
interactions.finding: Lightning Greaves and Swiftfoot Boots granting haste allow Tetsuo’s tap-cost activated ability to be used on the turn Tetsuo comes under your control. Greaves shroud does not interfere with the activation because the ability targets another creature, not Tetsuo.

interactions.name: Frozen Aether
interactions.finding: Opposing creatures enter tapped under Frozen Aether, so while they remain tapped they satisfy Tetsuo’s target condition.

interactions.name: Fumiko and Propaganda
interactions.finding: Fumiko requires opposing creatures to attack if able but does not force players to pay attack costs. Propaganda therefore still influences where forced/goaded creatures can attack; goad requirements are satisfied by attacking another player when able.

interactions.name: Sink into Stupor MDFC
interactions.finding: Soporific Springs is a land face and preserves a functional land slot. Sink into Stupor can return an opposing spell or nonland permanent to its owner’s hand; returning a spell this way does not counter it.
